newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus leader takes step back in a row with US.
newsitem.headline: Belarus leader takes step back in a row with US.

text.p: - Belarussian President Alexander Lukashenko took a step back in a row with the United States over an expelled diplomat, saying on Monday he wanted to strengthen relations with Washington.

"President Lukashenko underlined the importance of widening cooperation with the United States. He said that Belarus had enough political will to strengthen cooperation with the United States despite some difficulties," state television said in its late evening news.
The expulsion of U.S. diplomat Serzh Alexandrov, a first secretary at the embassy, prompted U.S. protests and a Minsk response earlier on Monday that Washington was behaving disrespectfully.

"We don't want people to say that there was an anti-American campaign in Belarus," Lukashenko was quoted as saying during a meeting with the newly-appointed Belarusssian Ambassador to the United States Valery Tsepkalo.
Alexandrov was arrested at an opposition rally where clashes broke out on Sunday, and was told to leave within 24 hours.
Meanwhile a Belarussian deputy foreign minister was quoted as saying that Belarus had no negative attitudes towards "such a powerful state" as the United States.
The U.S. State Department said on Monday that it might retaliate in response to its diplomat's expulsion from Belarus.
